issues.on_page: Total assets 6,369,523; total liabilities 1,382,378 + total net position 4,990,605 = 6,372,983
issues.issue: Confirmed this is the printed report's own error, not a misread or missed line. Every Total-column line on p1 matches the page and each section adds to its printed subtotal. The Business-type column prints restricted cash of 62,661 (total assets 2,281,322), but the proprietary Statement of Net Position (p6) prints 66,121 (Water 3,460 + Sewer 62,661) and total assets of 2,284,782, which equals business-type liabilities 766,559 + net position 1,518,223. So the Water Fund's 3,460 restricted cash (matching its 3,460 customer deposits) was left off p1. The figures stay as printed and the discrepancy is recorded correctly.

The page doesn't say where the grants come from (the Statement of Activities only says 'Operating grants and contributions'). They could be state or local money (intergovernmental/state aid). The same applies to the four detail Grants lines (detail[6], detail[13], detail[19], detail[23]). The extractor already marked these for review.
These are CDBG loan repayments, which are probably repayments of loan principal rather than revenue. No category fits exactly, so 'other' with review is defensible. The same applies to detail[78].

issues.on_page: Cemetery: Insurance 131, Transportation, meals, and lodging 170, Supplies 205 (total 506)
issues.issue: The category rules put cemetery under health/welfare. The extractor used streets/highways so the lines tie to the statement's 'Public works' 506 in the General Fund column (p5), which is defensible. The same applies to detail[65], detail[66] and the 506 inside disbursements[2] 'Public works' 66,568.
Sales tax collected and owed to the state could be classed as 'due to other governments'.
